changes: Add four safe internal-argument EmplaceValue adapters: const-reference and mutable-reference construction policies for Array1 and Array2, without Clone or Default bounds.

Validate source Value/ChangeValue argument before target shape; construct a distinct local temporary from the still-live source; reuse assign_emplaced to assign, destroy the temporary, then return the existing target.
Equal source/target indices still pass a distinct temporary to assignment. Source mutation during move construction remains visible on constructor failure and before target assignment.

Array2 target inherited ChangeAt validation remains after construction, matching the C++17 assignment RHS-before-LHS rule. A shortened actual target backing destroys its constructed temporary after the bounds error.
No original assertions or existing convenience replacement policies are changed.
probe_policy: The native payload records C/M copy/move construction, K before constructor completion, A before assignment, L after target and temporary mutation, X destruction, and R return. One hundred twenty rows cover both dimensions, owned/borrowed storage, const/move constructor arguments, both directions/self and five success/failure phases. Eighteen invalid-index rows distinguish source and target validation. Two shortened-target rows establish construction then target rejection then temporary destruction. Seven Rust tests consume all 140 native rows. Three Rust-only tests cover owned FnOnce callbacks, non-Default/non-Clone payloads and safe invalid source backing rejection.
limitations: These are adapters for native EmplaceValue compositions with Value/ChangeValue source arguments, not new C++ overloads. The two FunctionTemplate declaration bindings represent four Rust bodies; template-owned CXXMethod children and argument-dependency declarations earn no separate mapping credit.

The callback chooses constructor and move assignment semantics explicitly. Native overload resolution and arbitrary variadic combinations, including multiple internal arguments, require additional adapters or call policies.

Supported aliasing consists of one source element inside the same exclusive array view. Arbitrary raw overlap, independently overlapping wrappers, subobject aliases, constructor-retained pointers, callback reentry and retained references across exclusive borrows remain outside the claim.

Shared read-only targets retain their existing Rust detachment policy, outside native writable const-cast buffer equivalence. Owned and mutable-borrowed arrays preserve storage, source lifetime and target object lifetime.

Native Array2 Value/ChangeValue may access invalid storage after independently shortened inherited backing. Rust safely checks that source before target validation; those guard tests do not earn native parity credit. Native EmplaceValue target flat validation is defined and its after-construction order is covered.

Rust panic/native exception comparisons cover defined source/target state, operation ordering and destructor events. Throwing destructors, allocation hooks, raw constructor-failure leaks and uninitialized storage remain open.
Both array classes remain incomplete; global API inventory and original legacy-test mapping credit are unchanged.
